cards.q: 滚烫的锅上，水珠为何跳着舞不蒸发？
cards.short: 水珠靠蒸汽膜悬空
body: 德国医生莱顿弗罗斯特1756年在论文中描述此现象。当锅温远超水的沸点，超过约200摄氏度后，水珠不再贴锅面沸腾，而是悬空滑动数十秒。
水珠接触极热锅面的瞬间，底部薄层迅速汽化，垫出一层蒸汽膜。蒸汽导热能力远低于金属直接接触，使水珠悬浮其上，反而比中温锅蒸发得更慢。
常识认为锅越热水珠消失越快，但沸腾曲线在莱顿弗罗斯特点之后出现反常下凹：温度继续升高，水珠存活时间反而变长，这一区间称为膜态沸腾。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　高速摄影记录水珠在灼热锅面上悬浮滑动的瞬间。
cards.qe: Why does a water droplet dance on a scorching pan instead of evaporating?
cards.shorte: A vapor film levitates the droplet
cards.fige: Plate I. High-speed capture of a water droplet gliding on a superheated pan.
bodye: German physician Johann Gottlob Leidenfrost described the effect in a 1756 treatise. Once a pan's surface passes roughly 200 degrees Celsius, a water drop stops boiling flat against it and instead glides for tens of seconds.

On contact with the superheated surface, the drop's underside instantly vaporizes into a thin cushion of steam. Steam conducts heat far worse than direct metal contact, so the levitated drop evaporates more slowly than expected.

It seems obvious that a hotter pan evaporates water faster, but the boiling curve dips sharply at the Leidenfrost point: past it, rising temperature makes drops survive longer, a regime called film boiling.

cards.q: 巴塞罗那街区为何四角都切成八边形？
cards.short: 街区切角便于转弯
body: 巴塞罗那新城区街区呈方形切角的八边形，由工程师赛尔达于19世纪设计，是欧洲少见的规整网格城市。
切角扩大了十字路口空间，让马车与有轨电车转弯更顺畅，也为建筑增加了采光与通风角度。
这套设计常被当成纯粹的审美选择，实际首要目的是交通与卫生功能，美观只是附带结果。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　巴塞罗那新城区俯瞰，街区四角均被切平。
cards.src: 伊尔德方索·赛尔达《巴塞罗那扩建计划》
cards.qe: Why are the corners of Barcelona's city blocks cut off?
cards.shorte: Chamfered blocks ease traffic turns
cards.fige: Plate I. An aerial view of Barcelona's Eixample, its block corners sliced flat.
bodye: Barcelona's 19th-century Eixample district is laid out in octagonal blocks, squares with their corners cut off, designed by engineer Ildefons Cerdà.
The chamfers opened up intersections, giving horse carts and later trams room to turn and improving sightlines, while letting more light and air reach the buildings.
The shape is often read as a stylistic flourish, but its first purpose was traffic flow and sanitation; the elegant look was a side effect.
cards.srce: Ildefons Cerdà, Eixample Plan of Barcelona

cards.q: 为什么喝水压不住辣，牛奶却可以？
cards.short: 牛奶靠脂肪破解辣味
body: 辣椒素是脂溶性生物碱，不溶于水。全脂牛奶含约3%乳脂，实验中缓解辣感的效果明显优于常温清水。
辣椒素与舌部痛觉受体TRPV1结合产生灼烧感；牛奶中的酪蛋白能包裹并带走这种脂溶性分子，而水只能暂时冲淡，无法真正剥离受体。
很多人辣到流泪第一反应是灌水，实际只会把辣椒素冲到口腔更多部位，让灼烧感暂时扩散而非缓解。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　辣椒果实剖面与全脂牛奶对照图版。
cards.qe: Why doesn't water help with chili heat, but milk does?
cards.shorte: Milk's fat breaks the burn
cards.fige: Plate I　Chili pepper cross-section paired with a glass of whole milk.
bodye: Capsaicin is a fat-soluble alkaloid, barely soluble in water. Whole milk, roughly 3% fat, relieves the burn far better than plain water in sensory trials.
Capsaicin binds the TRPV1 heat receptor on the tongue. Casein in milk surrounds and carries away the fat-soluble molecule, while water only spreads it around without detaching it.
Reaching for water when chili burns is instinctive, but it mostly spreads capsaicin across more of the mouth, prolonging the sting rather than easing it.

cards.q: 大脑把口哨语言当成音乐处理吗？
cards.short: 口哨语言激活语言脑区
body: 西班牙加纳利群岛拉戈梅拉岛的居民用哨音「讲」西班牙语，隔着深谷仍可传出数公里，2009年被列入联合国教科文组织非物质文化遗产。
神经科学研究让土耳其同类哨语使用者做脑成像测试，发现大脑处理哨音时更多调用双侧脑区，不像普通语言那样几乎只依赖左半球。
口哨常被当成纯音乐信号，但脑区反应更接近语言而非曲调；哨语并非独立语言，只是把西班牙语音位改写成音高。

cards.src: 联合国教科文组织非物质文化遗产名录（2009）；京特库恩等，《当代生物学》（2015）
cards.qe: Does the brain treat whistled speech as music?
cards.shorte: Whistled speech lights up language regions
cards.fige: Plate I　La Gomera's ravines, across which whistled speech still carries.
bodye: Islanders on La Gomera in Spain's Canary Islands speak Spanish by whistling, a code audible across ravines for several kilometers. UNESCO listed it as intangible heritage in 2009.

Brain-imaging studies on a related whistled Turkish speech found listeners process the whistles with substantially more activity in both hemispheres, not the near-total left-brain dominance typical of ordinary speech.
Whistling is usually treated as a pure musical signal, yet the brain response resembles language more than melody. The whistling is not a separate language, only spoken Spanish recoded as pitch.

cards.q: 自由女神像最初是什么颜色？
cards.short: 女神像氧化后才变绿
body: 自由女神像1886年落成时，铜质外皮呈暗棕色，与今天所见的绿色完全不同。
女神像外皮为纯铜打造，铜在空气和海盐中缓慢氧化生成铜绿，这一过程持续了约二十至三十年。
许多人以为绿色是最初设计颜色，那层铜绿只是氧化的自然结果，并非人工上色。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　自由女神像铜质表皮特写，氧化生成的铜绿覆盖了原本的棕色。
cards.qe: What color was the Statue of Liberty originally?
cards.shorte: It only turned green after oxidizing
cards.fige: Plate I. A close-up of the Statue of Liberty's copper skin, its original brown hidden beneath a green patina.
bodye: When the Statue of Liberty was dedicated in 1886, its copper skin was a dark brown, nothing like the green it shows today.
The statue's copper surface slowly oxidized in air and sea salt, forming a green patina over roughly twenty to thirty years.
Many assume green was the original design, but that patina is simply the natural result of oxidation, not an applied color.

cards.q: 巨魔芋为何会发热又发臭？
cards.short: 发热助气味远播传粉
body: 巨魔芋开花时中央肉穗温度可升高至接近人体体温，比周围环境高出不少，同时释放类似腐肉的硫化物气味。
花序细胞线粒体高速氧化脂肪供能产热，这种代谢速率可与飞行中的蜂鸟相当，是植物界罕见的产热方式。
发热并非为了保暖，而是让恶臭分子更容易挥发扩散，专门吸引食腐甲虫与丽蝇替它传粉。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　巨魔芋开花时肉穗结构的植物学摄影。
cards.qe: Why does the titan arum heat up and reek?
cards.shorte: Heat helps its stench travel far
cards.fige: Plate I. A botanical photograph of the titan arum's spadix in bloom.
bodye: When the titan arum blooms, its central spadix can warm to near human body temperature, well above ambient air, while releasing sulfurous, carrion-like odors.
Mitochondria in the flower's cells rapidly oxidize fat for heat at a metabolic rate comparable to a hovering hummingbird — rare for a plant.
The heat isn't for warmth; it helps the stench molecules evaporate and spread further, drawing in carrion beetles and blowflies to pollinate it.

cards.q: 《神奈川冲浪里》标志性蓝色从何而来？
cards.short: 海浪蓝色是欧洲进口颜料
body: 《神奈川冲浪里》约作于1831年，画面中大面积使用普鲁士蓝，一种由柏林发明的化学合成颜料。
普鲁士蓝1704年在柏林被意外合成，19世纪经荷兰商船传入日本，因其色泽浓艳且价格低于天然群青，很快被浮世绘画师采用。
常被当作日本传统色的浮世绘海浪蓝，源头是欧洲实验室的化学发明，并非本土矿物颜料。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　葛饰北斋《神奈川冲浪里》中的普鲁士蓝浪涛。
cards.qe: Where did the iconic blue in The Great Wave come from?
cards.shorte: The wave's signature blue was a European import
cards.fige: Plate I. Prussian blue waves in Hokusai's Great Wave off Kanagawa.
bodye: The Great Wave off Kanagawa, made around 1831, uses broad passages of Prussian blue, a synthetic pigment invented in a chemistry lab, not ground from any mineral.
Prussian blue was accidentally synthesized in Berlin in 1704, then reached Japan in the 19th century via Dutch trading ships, prized for its vivid tone and lower cost than natural ultramarine.
Though treated as a native Japanese color, the wave's signature blue traces back to a European laboratory rather than any local mineral pigment.

cards.q: 海水的蓝色，是天空映出来的吗？
cards.short: 水分子吸收红光呈蓝
body: 纯水对红光的吸收强度是对蓝光的约百倍，光穿透十米水层后，红光已大幅衰减，蓝绿光相对保留更多。
水分子中氢氧键的振动频率恰好能吸收红外及可见光谱红端的光子，这是分子固有的振动吸收特性，与天空反射无关。
常见说法认为海水蓝色只是反射天空，但阴天海水依旧呈蓝；天空反射只影响水面高光，不改变水体本身颜色。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　深水蓝色与光谱吸收对照
cards.qe: Is the ocean's blue color just a reflection of the sky?
cards.shorte: Water absorbs red light, turns blue
cards.fige: Plate I. Deep blue water compared with its light-absorption spectrum
bodye: Pure water absorbs red light roughly a hundred times more strongly than blue light. After passing through about ten meters of water, red light is largely gone while blue and green remain.

The vibration frequency of water's O-H bonds happens to absorb photons at the red end of the visible spectrum and beyond into the infrared — an intrinsic molecular property, unrelated to any reflection of the sky.
Ocean blue is often assumed to be a mirror of the sky, but the sea stays blue even under overcast skies. Sky reflection only adds surface glare — it doesn't change the water's own color.

cards.q: 冥王星和卡戎谁才是中心？
cards.short: 冥王星与卡戎互绕运行
body: 卡戎质量约为冥王星的八分之一，是太阳系中卫星与主星质量之比最大的一对，两者质心因此落在冥王星地表之外。
两颗星体绕共同质心公转，周期约6.4天，且都已被彼此潮汐锁定，从冥王星表面某点看，卡戎几乎悬停不动。
地月系统里只有月球单向锁定地球，冥王星却双向锁定；假如站在冥王星背对卡戎的一面，将永远看不到这颗卫星。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　新视野号拍摄的冥王星与卡戎合照
cards.src: 新视野号冥王星系统研究
cards.qe: Between Pluto and Charon, which one is the center?
cards.shorte: Pluto and Charon orbit one another
cards.fige: Plate I. New Horizons' portrait of Pluto and Charon together
bodye: Charon's mass is about one-eighth of Pluto's, the largest moon-to-primary ratio of any round-body pair in the solar system, so their shared center of mass lies in space beyond Pluto's surface.
Rather than Charon circling a stationary Pluto, both bodies orbit that shared point every 6.4 days, and each is tidally locked to the other, so Charon hovers almost motionless in Pluto's sky.
Unlike Earth and the Moon, where only the Moon is locked, Pluto is locked to Charon too; standing on Pluto's far side, facing away from Charon, one would never see it at all.

cards.q: 潜水民族的脾脏为何格外大？
cards.short: 脾脏是潜水的氧气罐
body: 印尼巴瑶族世代潜水采集为生，2018年一项研究发现，其脾脏体积比邻近陆居族群平均大五成左右。
脾脏收缩时会把储存的红细胞压入血液，提升血氧携带能力，这种收缩反应在潜水民族中更强更快。
差异并非后天训练所致，基因分析显示，巴瑶族携带一种影响甲状腺激素的基因变异，脾脏增大是遗传适应。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　人体脾脏在腹腔中的解剖位置图。
cards.src: 《潜水民族的生理与基因适应研究》
cards.qe: Why are sea-diving peoples' spleens so large?
cards.shorte: Spleen as a dive tank
cards.fige: Plate I. Anatomical position of the spleen within the human abdominal cavity.
bodye: Indonesia's Bajau people have dived for generations to gather food. A 2018 study found their spleens run roughly fifty percent larger than neighboring land-based groups.
A contracting spleen forces stored red blood cells into circulation, raising blood oxygen capacity. This contraction reflex is stronger and faster in diving populations.
The difference is not just training. Genetic analysis found the Bajau carry a variant affecting thyroid hormone regulation, meaning the larger spleen is an inherited adaptation.
cards.srce: Physiological and Genetic Adaptations to Diving in Sea Nomads

cards.q: 威尼斯的房子为何建在木桩上不腐烂？
cards.short: 木桩泡水数百年不朽
body: 威尼斯建筑地基由数以百万计的木桩打入潟湖淤泥支撑，多为赤杨木，部分木桩已在水下伫立数百年。
淤泥隔绝了氧气，缺氧环境抑制了分解木材的真菌与细菌，木质纤维反而随年代增加逐渐矿化变硬。
木桩并非因泡水而腐坏，真正的隐患是水位下降后露出空气，接触氧气才开始朽坏。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　里亚尔托桥下的木桩地基结构。
cards.srcMeta: 世界遗产保护报告，1987年起
cards.qe: Why don't Venice's wooden pile foundations rot underwater?
cards.shorte: Submerged piles harden instead of rotting
cards.fige: Plate I. The wooden pile foundations beneath the Rialto Bridge.
bodye: Venice's buildings stand on millions of wooden piles, mostly alder, driven into the lagoon's mud; some have stood submerged for centuries.
The mud seals out oxygen, starving the fungi and bacteria that break down wood, so the fibers slowly mineralize and harden instead of decaying.
The piles do not rot from being wet; the real danger comes when falling water levels expose them to air, which is when decay actually begins.

cards.q: 古埃及工人罢工要求什么？
cards.short: 史上最早罢工为讨口粮
body: 公元前1152年左右，拉美西斯三世在位第29年，代尔麦地那陵墓工匠因谷物口粮迟发多日，放下工具停工，前往邻近神庙静坐抗议。
工匠薪酬不发现金，全靠国家配给的谷物和啤酒维生，粮仓管理疏漏或运输延误就意味着全家断粮，工匠遂以停工向上级施压，事件被记入纸草档案。
这场停工是已知最早的劳工罢工记录，工匠并非奴隶而是拿国家俸禄的专业匠人，抗议目标始终是足额发粮，而非改善建墓本身的劳动条件。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　都灵博物馆藏《罢工纸草》记录代尔麦地那工匠停工经过的僧侣体文字。
cards.qe: What did ancient Egyptian workers demand when they went on strike?
cards.shorte: History's first strike was over grain
cards.fige: Plate I. Hieratic text on the Turin Strike Papyrus recording the Deir el-Medina work stoppage.
bodye: Around 1152 BCE, in year 29 of Ramesses III, tomb builders at Deir el-Medina saw their grain rations arrive late, downed their tools, and marched to nearby temples to sit in protest.

Workers were paid in grain and beer rather than cash, so any lapse in the storehouse or delayed delivery meant hunger for their families; the stoppage was recorded on papyrus by officials forced to respond.
This is the earliest documented labor strike on record. The men were salaried craftsmen, not slaves, and their sole demand throughout was full, on-time rations rather than better working conditions.

cards.q: 哪种植物的叶片能承受人的重量？
cards.short: 王莲叶片靠肋状结构承重
body: 王莲(Victoria amazonica)叶片直径可达3米,边缘卷起如盘,若重量均匀分布,单张叶片可承受约45公斤而不下沉。
叶背密布放射状粗壮叶脉与横向支撑肋,内部充气组织增加浮力,把压强分散到整张叶面,类似天然桁架结构。
承重前提是重量必须均匀分摊,常借助木板等分散点压力;若人直接单脚踩踏集中受力,叶片会迅速刺穿下沉,并非可以随意站立。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　王莲巨大圆叶漂浮水面照片,展示放射状叶脉支撑结构。
cards.src: 英国皇家植物园(邱园)物种档案
cards.qe: Which plant's leaf can support the weight of a person?
cards.shorte: Victoria's ribbed leaf spreads out the load
cards.fige: Plate I  Photograph of a giant Victoria water lily leaf afloat, showing its radiating rib structure.
bodye: The giant water lily Victoria amazonica grows leaves up to three meters across with an upturned rim; when weight is spread evenly, a single leaf can support roughly 45 kilograms without sinking.
The underside carries thick radiating veins and cross-ribs, with air-filled tissue adding buoyancy. Together they spread pressure across the whole leaf like a natural truss.
The catch is that weight must be distributed evenly, usually with a board; step directly on one spot and the leaf punctures and sinks at once, it is no platform for casual standing.

cards.q: 兵马俑出土时为何迅速褪色？
cards.short: 兵马俑出土数分钟内掉色
body: 秦始皇陵兵马俑出土时多带彩绘，但陶俑表面的生漆底层暴露在干燥空气中后，数分钟内便开始卷曲剥落，颜色迅速消失。
生漆层此前长期埋藏在稳定的湿度环境里，出土后湿度骤降导致漆层收缩变形，附着其上的矿物颜料随之脱落，与陶胎本身关系不大。
许多人以为兵马俑本就是陶土本色，事实是几乎每尊出土时都曾色彩鲜明，褪色是保存条件突变造成的后果。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　出土初期尚存彩绘痕迹的兵马俑陶俑。
cards.src: 兵马俑彩绘保护研究报告
cards.qe: Why did the Terracotta Army lose its color so quickly after excavation?
cards.shorte: Color vanished within minutes of excavation
cards.fige: Plate I. A terracotta figure with surviving paint shortly after excavation.
bodye: Many Terracotta Army figures emerged from the pit richly painted, but once their lacquer ground was exposed to dry air, it began curling and flaking within minutes, taking the color with it.

The lacquer layer had sat in a stable, humid burial environment for over two thousand years; the sudden drop in humidity after excavation makes it shrink and warp, dislodging the mineral pigments bound to it.

The figures are often assumed to have always been bare clay, but nearly every one was vividly painted when unearthed — the color loss is a side effect of the sudden change in conditions, not their original state.

cards.q: 镜子把左右换了，还是把前后换了？
cards.short: 镜像本质是前后翻转
body: 把写有文字的纸对着镜子，文字左右颠倒但上下不变；这一现象几乎人人从小观察过，却极少被准确解释。
镜面只反转与镜面垂直的那一个方向，即前后方向；人转身面对镜子时，是自己把左右轴也一并转了个方向，造成左右颠倒的错觉。
若把镜子放在头顶或脚下，颠倒的会变成上下而非左右；镜子并不偏爱左右，颠倒方向完全取决于观察者与镜面的相对朝向。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　镜中镜像文字对照
cards.qe: Does a mirror swap left and right, or front and back?
cards.shorte: A mirror flips front-to-back, not sides
cards.fige: Plate I. Mirror-reversed text compared with the original
bodye: Hold a page of text up to a mirror and the letters reverse left to right while staying upright — a sight nearly everyone has seen since childhood, yet rarely explained correctly.

A mirror only reverses the axis perpendicular to its surface — front to back. When a person turns to face the mirror, they rotate their own left-right axis, which creates the illusion of a left-right swap.

Place the mirror overhead or underfoot instead, and the reversal becomes up-down, not left-right. A mirror has no preference for any direction — which way things flip depends entirely on the viewer's orientation.
cards.query: Leonardo da Vinci mirror writing manuscript

cards.q: 巧克力表面泛白霜，是发霉变质了吗？
cards.short: 泛白是脂肪析出非发霉
body: 巧克力反复经历约5摄氏度以上的温度波动后，表面常析出细小白色结晶，业内称为起霜，并非霉菌滋生。
巧克力中的可可脂具有多种结晶形态，温度波动会使脂肪重新熔化再结晶，析出的脂肪或糖分迁移到表面形成白色薄层。
很多人看到白霜就整块丢弃，起霜多数只影响外观与口感，风味和安全性通常不受影响，仍可安全食用。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　巧克力块体表面标本图版。
cards.qe: Is the white bloom on chocolate mold?
cards.shorte: White bloom is fat, not mold
cards.fige: Plate I　Specimen of a chocolate bar's surface.
bodye: After chocolate cycles through temperature swings of roughly 5°C or more, fine white crystals often surface — the industry calls this bloom, not mold.
Cocoa butter crystallizes in several different forms; temperature swings melt and re-form the fat, and the migrating fat or sugar forms a thin white layer.
Many people toss chocolate the moment it turns white, but bloom usually only changes texture and looks — flavor and safety are typically unaffected.

cards.q: 老式中文打字机上有键盘吗？
cards.short: 字盘检字，不用键盘
body: 民国至1980年代常见的中文打字机没有字母键盘，字台上平铺约两千多个常用汉字字模，打字员移动选字杆逐字挑出后击印上纸。
汉字数量庞大，无法像拉丁字母那样压缩进几十个按键；工程师转而把常用字铺成网格，用检索代替按键，速度靠肌肉记忆练出来。
熟练打字员默记字模方位，手速可媲美西文打字机；生僻字备用字盘另存，需要时现拣现装，并非每个汉字都常驻机上。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　双鸽牌中文打字机字盘与选字机构实物。
cards.src: Thomas S. Mullaney《中文打字机：一部历史》，麻省理工学院出版社（2017）
cards.qe: Did old Chinese typewriters have a keyboard?
cards.shorte: A character tray stood in for the keyboard
cards.fige: Plate I　The character tray and selector arm of a Chinese typewriter.
bodye: Chinese typewriters common from the Republican era into the 1980s had no letter keyboard. A flat bed held roughly two thousand common character types; the typist swept a selector arm across the grid, picked a character, and struck it onto the page.

Chinese has too many characters to compress into a few dozen keys the way Latin alphabets can. Engineers instead laid the common characters out in a grid and replaced key-pressing with searching; speed came from muscle memory.

Skilled typists memorized the map of the tray and could work nearly as fast as a Western typewriter. Rare characters lived on supplementary trays, fetched and swapped in only when needed, not every character sat on the machine at once.
cards.srce: Thomas S. Mullaney, The Chinese Typewriter: A History, MIT Press (2017)

cards.q: 人类怎么「看见」系外行星？
cards.short: 首颗系外行星靠摆动现身
body: 1995年，两位瑞士天文学家确认飞马座51b，是首颗环绕类日恒星的系外行星，公转周期仅4.2天，比水星近得多。
行星本身太暗难以直接看到，天文学家转而测量恒星光谱线的周期性红移蓝移，那是行星引力拉扯恒星摆动留下的痕迹。
当时的行星形成理论认为，气态巨行星只应诞生在远离恒星之处，这颗近距离气态行星的发现改写了理论，两人于2019年获诺贝尔物理学奖。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　飞马座51b与母恒星的艺术想象图
cards.qe: How did astronomers first detect a planet they could never actually see?
cards.shorte: First exoplanet found through starlight wobble
cards.fige: Plate I. Artist's impression of 51 Pegasi b and its host star
bodye: In 1995, two Swiss astronomers confirmed 51 Pegasi b, the first exoplanet found orbiting a Sun-like star; it circles its star in just 4.2 days, far closer than Mercury orbits the Sun.
The planet itself was too faint to see directly, so astronomers instead measured periodic shifts in the star's spectral lines, the telltale wobble caused by the planet's gravity tugging on its star.

Planet-formation theory at the time held that gas giants should only form far from their star; this close-orbiting giant forced a rethink, and the discovery earned its authors the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.

cards.q: 中世纪欧洲修道院为何养鱼塘？
cards.short: 为常年斋戒日常备鲜鱼
body: 中世纪基督教历法一年中近半天数禁食肉类，从每周五到长达四十天的大斋期，修道院便挖掘阶梯式池塘养殖鲤鱼等淡水鱼备用。
许多修道院远离海岸和渔场，运输鲜鱼困难，僧侣利用溪流筑坝分级建塘，把鱼苗、育成鱼和待食成鱼分池饲养，形成可持续的鱼塘系统。
这类鱼塘并非修行清苦的象征，而是精密的水产工程：西多会等修会绘制引水图纸管理水位，鲤鱼因耐低氧、易于越冬成为最常见的养殖鱼种。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　芳廷斯修道院阶梯式鱼塘与引水渠遗址照片。
cards.src: 芳廷斯修道院鱼塘遗址
cards.qe: Why did medieval European monasteries keep fish ponds?
cards.shorte: Ponds kept fish ready for fast days
cards.fige: Plate I. Ruins of Fountains Abbey's terraced stew ponds and water leat.
bodye: The medieval Christian calendar barred meat on nearly half the year's days, from every Friday to the forty days of Lent, so monasteries dug terraced ponds to raise carp and other freshwater fish.

Many monasteries sat far from coasts and fisheries where fresh fish was hard to transport, so monks dammed streams into graded ponds, keeping fry, growing fish, and ready-to-eat stock in separate pools.

These ponds were not a sign of ascetic poverty but of precise water engineering: orders such as the Cistercians drew up leat diagrams to manage water levels, and carp became the standard stock for tolerating low oxygen and overwintering well.

cards.q: 啄木鸟头骨真的能缓震吗？
cards.short: 啄木鸟头骨异常坚硬
body: 啄木鸟啄击树干时，头部瞬间减速可达约1200倍重力，持续不足一毫秒，每日啄击可达数千次。
2022年比利时研究团队发现，啄木鸟头骨并非弹性缓冲垫，而是坚硬结构，几乎不吸收冲击；大脑不受伤，靠的是脑体积小、与颅骨贴合紧密，冲击应变被分散。
此前认为头骨像缓冲垫一样吸震，这项研究推翻了这一说法——若头骨真能大幅缓冲，啄击效率反而会下降，不利于凿开树皮觅食。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　啄木鸟凿击树干的姿态照片。
cards.srcMeta: Van Wassenbergh 等，比利时安特卫普大学，2022年
cards.qe: Does a woodpecker's skull actually cushion the impact?
cards.shorte: Woodpecker skull is unusually stiff
cards.fige: Plate I. Photograph of a woodpecker pecking at a tree trunk.
bodye: When a woodpecker strikes wood, its head decelerates by roughly 1,200 g in under a millisecond, up to several thousand times a day.

A 2022 Belgian study found the skull is not an elastic cushion but a rigid structure that absorbs almost no shock; the brain stays safe because it is small and tightly packed, spreading out the strain.
Textbooks long assumed the skull cushions each blow. The study overturned that: a truly shock-absorbing skull would blunt each strike, making it harder to chisel through bark.
cards.srcMetae: Van Wassenbergh et al., University of Antwerp, 2022

cards.q: 梵高生前的画作卖得怎么样？
cards.short: 一生只卖出一幅油画
body: 梵高在世时共创作约860幅油画，加上素描等作品逾2000件，但生前有记录的售出画作只有一幅——《红色葡萄园》。
他的画风在当时被视为色彩过于强烈、笔触过于潦草，不符合主流市场趣味，画商与藏家大多不愿收购。
他去世后画价一路攀升，如今单幅作品拍卖价可达数千万美元，与生前几乎无人问津的境况形成鲜明反差。
cards.fig: 图版 Ⅰ　梵高《红色葡萄园》，他生前唯一售出的画作。
cards.src: 梵高书信项目及馆藏研究
cards.srcMeta: 梵高博物馆，阿姆斯特丹
cards.qe: How did Van Gogh's paintings sell during his lifetime?
cards.shorte: He sold only one painting in his life
cards.fige: Plate I. Van Gogh's The Red Vineyard, the only painting he sold in his lifetime.
bodye: Van Gogh made roughly 860 oil paintings and over 2,000 works in total during his decade as an artist, yet only one sale is documented in his lifetime — The Red Vineyard.
His color was seen as too intense and his brushwork too loose for contemporary taste, so dealers and collectors mostly passed on his work.
Prices climbed steeply after his death; single paintings now sell for tens of millions of dollars, a stark contrast to the near-total silence around his work while he was alive.

cards.q: 闪电比太阳表面还热，为何很少点燃周围空气？
cards.short: 闪电瞬时温度超太阳表面
body: 闪电通道瞬间温度可达约三万摄氏度，接近太阳表面温度（约五千五百摄氏度）的五倍以上，是地球上自然产生的最高温之一。
闪电放电通道极窄，持续时间仅几十微秒，传递的总热能有限；空气受热迅速膨胀又冷却，来不及把足够能量传给周围物体。
人们常把温度等同于烧灼能力，但物体是否被点燃取决于总热量与接触时间；闪电确会引燃干草和树木，只是概率远低于直觉预期。

cards.qe: Lightning is hotter than the Sun's surface — why doesn't it torch everything nearby?
cards.shorte: Lightning briefly outheats the Sun
cards.fige: Plate I. High-speed photograph of a lightning discharge channel
bodye: A lightning channel can briefly reach about 30,000°C — more than five times the Sun's surface temperature of roughly 5,500°C, making it among the hottest things that occur naturally on Earth.

The discharge channel is extremely narrow and lasts only tens of microseconds, so the total heat delivered stays limited. Air heats and expands almost instantly, then cools before much energy can transfer to nearby objects.

Temperature is often equated with scorching power, but whether something ignites depends on total heat and contact time. Lightning does start grass and tree fires — just far less often than the temperature alone would suggest.

cards.q: 手指甲和脚趾甲谁长得快？
cards.short: 指甲比脚趾甲长得快
body: 手指甲平均每月生长约三毫米，脚趾甲只有其三分之一左右，速度还因手指、年龄和季节而不同。
手指使用越频繁，局部血液循环和微小机械刺激越多，越能促进甲床细胞分裂，所以惯用手指甲长得更快。
常有人以为剪得越勤长得越快，这颠倒了因果；真正决定速度的是血流与甲床细胞分裂节律，与修剪无关。

cards.qe: Which grows faster, fingernails or toenails?
cards.shorte: Fingernails grow faster
cards.fige: Plate I. Comparative anatomy of finger and toe nail-bed structures.
bodye: Fingernails grow about three millimeters a month on average, roughly three times faster than toenails. Growth speed also shifts with the finger, age, and season.
Growth rate tracks local blood circulation and use. Fingers stay active and sit closer to the heart, so nutrient delivery is richer, which speeds up the dominant hand's nails.
Many assume frequent trimming speeds growth, but that reverses cause and effect. Growth is set by blood flow and nail-bed cell division, not by cutting.

cards.q: 波特兰和盐湖城，谁的街区更大？
cards.short: 盐湖城街区超波特兰十倍
body: 波特兰标准街区约61米见方，盐湖城街区约201米见方，面积相差约十一倍，是美国城市规划反差最大的实例之一。
波特兰刻意采用小街区，增加临街转角地价并提升步行友好度；盐湖城依照摩门教徒的「锡安城规划」，为每户预留大地块建房和种菜。
两座城市建城时间相近，却因规划理念不同形成悬殊的街区尺度；盐湖城的大街区如今也带来了步行距离过长的新问题。

cards.qe: Portland or Salt Lake City: whose blocks are bigger?
cards.shorte: Salt Lake City's blocks dwarf Portland's
cards.fige: Plate I. An aerial view of a Salt Lake City block, far larger than a typical city block.
bodye: A standard Portland block runs about 61 meters per side; a Salt Lake City block runs about 201 meters, roughly eleven times the area, one of the starkest contrasts in American city planning.

Portland deliberately kept blocks small to multiply valuable corner lots and keep streets walkable; Salt Lake City followed the Mormon settlers' Plat of Zion, which reserved large lots for houses and gardens.
The two cities were founded only decades apart, yet ended up with wildly different block scales; Salt Lake City's oversized blocks now make some downtown walks surprisingly long.

cards.q: 下午三点喝的咖啡，为什么凌晨还睡不着？
cards.short: 咖啡因五小时消耗一半
body: 咖啡因进入血液后，人体清除一半约需五小时；一杯咖啡若在下午三点喝下，到晚上八点体内仍残留约一半咖啡因。
咖啡因主要经肝脏细胞色素酶代谢分解，血液浓度随时间大致按指数曲线下降，个体代谢速度受基因和肝功能影响而有差异。
很多人以为咖啡因几小时就代谢干净，按五小时半衰期计算，一杯咖啡的影响往往要十小时以上才基本消退。

cards.qe: You drink coffee at 3pm — why are you still awake at midnight?
cards.shorte: Caffeine's half-life is 5 hours
cards.fige: Plate I　Curve of caffeine blood concentration decaying over time.
bodye: The body clears about half of any dose of caffeine in roughly five hours. Coffee drunk at 3pm still leaves about half its caffeine on board by 8pm.
Caffeine is broken down mainly by liver enzymes, and blood concentration falls in a roughly exponential curve; genetics and liver function shift the rate person to person.
People often assume caffeine clears in a few hours, but at a five-hour half-life, one cup's effects commonly linger past the ten-hour mark before fading.

cards.q: 金星的自转方向和其他行星相反吗？
cards.short: 金星自转方向与其他行星相反
body: 金星是太阳系中唯一自东向西逆向自转的大行星，其他七颗行星均自西向东旋转。金星自转一周需要约243个地球日，而公转周期仅225个地球日，导致其一天比一年还长。
主流理论认为金星早期曾遭受一次或多次大型天体撞击，改变了原有自转方向。另一种假说指出金星浓密大气层与太阳引力潮汐的长期作用可能逐步减慢并逆转了自转。
由于逆向自转，金星上太阳从西方升起，东方落下。但因金星表面被厚重云层永久遮蔽，实际上无法直接看到太阳的升落。

cards.qe: Does Venus rotate in the opposite direction to other planets?
cards.shorte: Venus rotates backward compared to other planets
bodye: Venus is the only major planet in the solar system that rotates east to west, opposite to the other seven planets. One Venusian rotation takes about 243 Earth days, while its orbital period is only 225 Earth days, making a day longer than a year.

The leading theory suggests Venus experienced one or more massive impacts early in its history that reversed its original rotation. An alternative hypothesis proposes that Venus's thick atmosphere and solar tidal forces gradually slowed and reversed its spin over time.

Due to retrograde rotation, the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east on Venus. However, the planet's surface is permanently shrouded by thick clouds, making direct observation of sunrise or sunset impossible.
